issue.title: Prevent unnecessary Quarkus restarts in nested tests

body: https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/46118 should fix this, but I've opened it as a draft to see if CI passed on my fork

> [#46118](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/46118) should fix this, but I've opened it as a draft to see if CI passed on my fork

I used your repo in my app and all my tests passed. And it seems that the app does not start/stop multiple times per nested test.

I got another question, now, when i run in total 3 tests, the console output has 4 times that the app stopped. (way less than before). Maybe when the test starts, it starts the app, then it sees that there are nested tests and it stops the first instance. Then, it continues with the normal procedure for the other tests (where we see that 3 times the app stopped).

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/821b7090-3b27-4bb8-938f-0dbdb5fe74e4)
That happpens because the outer class `ManifestTest` could itself contain tests that need to be run
@geoand can't we figure this out? I mean is the fact that there are no tests in the parent class something we can detect?
We could approximate it, but I don't think it's worth the effort (unless someone shows me a real world example where it makes a difference)

It could make sense, at the moment in my logs i see that Flyway migrations get executed 4 times.

And in fact i just added `SELECT pg_sleep(3);` to sleep my migration script for 3 seconds and the tests got  slower, even for the outer class which does not have any test.
@gbourant can you try https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/46118 again? I had to change the way things are done

@geoand, the tests are passing, but I noticed that the Flyway migrations run four times instead of three. Additionally, the number of times the app instance stops varies depending on how I run the tests, when running them from the IDE, it stops four times, but when building my Maven multi-module project, it stops three times. This might be because the inner tests exists in the last Maven module or because that inner tests runs first in the last module.
Yeah, that's expected but can probably be improved further later
